extracted.intended_audience: corporate investor-relations teams, press-release writers, financial communicators, financial journalists, and disclosure/regulatory analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing periodic narrative disclosures (MD&A, 10-K/10-Q, annual/sustainability reports, periodic press releases) so that year-over-year textual modification reflects real underlying change and is informative to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification-as-information
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeating last year's text verbatim signals 'no change worth reporting.' A press release that re-uses last quarter's language wholesale is correctly read by investors as low-information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reuse of prior-period language as an explicit signal to investors that nothing materially changed in that narrative segment. Avoid verbatim carryover when the underlying business has changed; meaningful textual change should accompany substantive change. Empirical finding: modification scores correlate with substantive economic change and with stock-price response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential-update discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: When the underlying business has materially changed, the press release should visibly update its narrative segments — not just the numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update narrative passages (explanations, product/market descriptions, forward-looking language) to reflect real changes. Don't rely solely on updated quantitative disclosures; investors expect corresponding narrative adjustments. Visible, segment-level changes help signal which parts of the business have changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer is not better. Brown–Tucker show that growing length without growing modification is negatively informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid adding verbosity or filler text that increases length but adds no new information. Monitor both length and substantive modification; increases in length should be accompanied by commensurate increases in novel, relevant content. Excessive length with little new language can reduce informativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosine-distance pre-publication audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before release, run a cosine-similarity check against the prior period's release; flag any segment with similarity above ~0.95 for review (is the underlying truly unchanged?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use text-similarity tooling (cosine similarity) as an audit: compute segment-level similarity to last period's language and automatically flag high-similarity passages for manual review. Suggested threshold: ~0.95 similarity as a starting point to identify near-verbatim reuse. Determine whether high similarity is appropriate (genuine unchanged facts/boilerplate) or a problematic recycling that should be revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: New-language flag
rubrics_metrics.description: When new product, market, regulatory, or risk-factor language enters the release, foreground it — investors weight new language more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly highlight or call out genuinely new narrative content (e.g., new product descriptions, new markets entered, new regulatory developments). Placement and prominence matter because investors treat novel language as a signal of new information; make new-language content easy to find and interpret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark genuinely-recurring boilerplate (safe harbor, 'About' section) clearly so investors can filter it out and focus on substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segregate and label boilerplate text so that similarity checks and readers can distinguish it from substantive narrative. Standard sections (company description, routine safe-harbor statements) should be consistently identified to avoid false positives in modification metrics and to reduce reader effort in finding substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-factor evolution disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When risk factors change, the release should highlight the change rather than burying it in tracked-changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly disclose and summarize how risk factors have evolved year-over-year; do not merely append or minimally edit prior wording. Make the nature and implications of changed risks clear and visible so investors can assess their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-over-year comparison block
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit Y/Y comparison block that quantifies the change rather than requiring investors to compute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a dedicated section that summarizes and quantifies the principal year-over-year narrative and operational changes (e.g., 'What changed and why' with bullet points or a short table). This reduces investor search costs and makes substantive differences obvious, increasing pickup-worthiness and the likelihood of substantive coverage.
